The wrapper classes, the href, the Cancel classes, and the Cancel text are byte-identical. `grep` confirms these are the only four occurrences of `mt-6 flex justify-end gap-4` in the repo, so the finding's occurrence count is complete. ## Scoping caveat: this is two extractions, not one `final-example` and `starter-example` are **independent Next.js apps** with their own `package.json` and their own `@/` alias root. There's no shared package between them, so a single component can't legitimately serve all four call sites — the fix is one `FormActions` per app, each consolidating its own create/edit pair. Cross-app consolidation would require inventing a shared UI package, which is a much larger change than the finding warrants (and would fight the fixture's intent, where the two apps are deliberately parallel copies). ## Proposed shared component New file in each app, next to the existing `button.tsx`: - `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/form-actions.tsx` - `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/form-actions.tsx` ```tsx import Link from 'next/link'; import { Button } from '@/app/ui/button'; export function FormActions({ cancelHref, submitLabel, cancelLabel = 'Cancel', children, }: { cancelHref: string; submitLabel: string; cancelLabel?: string; children?: React.ReactNode; }) { return (
{children} {cancelLabel}
); } ``` ### Public API **Props** | Prop | Type | Required | Why | |---|---|---|---| | `cancelHref` | `string` | yes | The one value that would genuinely differ on reuse (a customers form cancels to `/dashboard/customers`). Baking `/dashboard/invoices` in would hide a route inside a generic UI component. | | `submitLabel` | `string` | yes | The only token that actually varies today — "Create Invoice" / "Edit Invoice". | | `cancelLabel` | `string` | no, default `'Cancel'` | Identical at all four sites; a default keeps the call sites to one meaningful prop. | **Slots** | Slot | Type | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `children` | `ReactNode` | Leading action slot, rendered before Cancel. Absent at all four current call sites; it exists so a destructive action ("Delete invoice") can be added to the edit form without reopening the component's prop surface. | **Deliberately not props:** `className` on the wrapper, and the Cancel link's styling. Making those configurable re-opens the exact drift this extraction closes — the component owns the layout, callers own the labels and the destination. ### Call sites after the change ```tsx ``` ## Files that change **New (2):** - `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/form-actions.tsx` - `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/form-actions.tsx` **Edited (4)** — replace the 9-line subtree with the one-line call; drop the now-unused `Link` import where nothing else in the file uses it (all four import `Link` solely for this footer, so the import goes in each): - `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/invoices/create-form.tsx` (142–150) - `dashboard/final-example/app/ui/invoices/edit-form.tsx` (152–160) - `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/invoices/create-form.tsx` (101–109) - `dashboard/starter-example/app/ui/invoices/edit-form.tsx` (112–120) `Button` stays imported only in `form-actions.tsx`; the form files drop it too. ## Two things to expect on the next scan 1. **`crime_00064` clears** — the shape drops to one occurrence per app, below the detector's threshold. 2. **A new `exact_duplicate_block` may appear** for the two `form-actions.tsx` files, since they're identical across the two apps.
